changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6310-designer-formula-key-retired.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `designer.field.formula` (`'Formula (CEL)'`) in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, a different and live key belonging to metadata-admin's `ObjectFieldInspector` — the surface that still authors formula expressions.

### `.changeset/6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`

- names `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Both marketplace chunks were held by CHUNK CO-TENANCY, not by any import of the page: rolldown had parked `components/SuggestedBindingsPanel.tsx` (statically imported by the eager `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) in the first, and `console/marketplace/InstalledListWidget.tsx` (bare-imported by the package barrel for its SDUI registration) in the second. An `app-shell-eager-leaves` group in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` isolates those co-tenants so the three declared-lazy pages chunk by their own dynamic-only reachability. The console eager closure moves 3180.2 KB → 3171.5 KB gzipped (−8,888 bytes, 48 → 45 eager chunks) with the three per-chunk ceilings unmoved.

### `.changeset/7125-dashboard-empty-state-keys-retired.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `table.noRows` (`'No rows to display'`) and `engine.form.noRows` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, read at `widgets.tsx`) — two different, same-named keys in different namespaces. Nor the comments in `WidgetEmptyState.tsx`, `DatasetWidget.tsx`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and `PivotTable.tsx` that record WHY three widgets with three strings became one shared empty state; the packs' own comment keeps that rationale and now names the retirement instead of a row that is gone.

### `.changeset/8632-malformed-picklist-option-loud.md`

- names `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Two new strings land in the designer's own `en` / `zh` tables — the metadata-admin console owns its strings in `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` and is deliberately outside the ten locale packs (`packages/i18n/README.md`, "Scope — the `engine.*` carve-out").

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `af9e9572c` (merge-base with origin/main): 14 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1835 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2446 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36764873464)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `436a74e8058c67376c28349bfdf7c90dab1e68b1`
Local-runs: none

PR objectui#11259 (card objectui#11196, slice 2, `Fixes #11196`), judged against the card's body and its seven comments (triage `5909773493`, claim `5915720438`, ACCEPT `5915086680` answers 1 to 3, dev report `5918098195`), the PR body, its 15-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the head's check-runs. Files at the head were read through the contents API and one tarball of the head, grepped in scratch: nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**One rule, not a second ladder — right.** `resolveSurface` and `findSurfaceInTree` take an optional trailing `NavTargetLabelResolver` and name the leaf through slice 1's `navEntryLabelText`, which calls `@object-ui/layout`'s `resolveNavItemLabel`; no `??` chain and no target-key read is restated. The head has exactly three production callers, all in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` — the `NavTree` row, the load's first-leaf pick, the `?surface=` restore — and each passes the resolver, so no caller is left on the machine-name rung. `StudioNavItemInspector`'s field is `navItemLabelText` as value, `inheritedNavEntryText` as placeholder, `renamedLabel` / `clearedLabel` on edit: the same three functions `AppNavInspector.commitLabel` uses at the head, line for line. Both designers and the runtime branch on `label === undefined` (layout's `resolveNavItemLabel` and `navEntryLabelText` alike), so an empty map or `''` is a present label on every surface — the one absence test.

**The load effect and Commandment #10 — right.** `InterfacesPillar` holds `useNavTargetLabel()` in `targetLabelRef`, refreshed by a deps-less effect declared before the load effect; the load effect's dependency list stays `[client, packageId, publishNonce, draftNonce, metadataRefreshNonce]`, and `resolveTarget = targetLabelRef.current` is read after the load's awaits. The hook's `useMemo` identity is neither a dependency nor a key, and a re-run that rehydrates the nav edit buffer is not caused by a resolver change. `NavTree` and `StudioNavItemInspector` call the resolver during render, with no identity read. `AppNavCanvas.addItem` adds `targetLabel` to its `useCallback` list: named right as the fresh-closure direction — a discarded memo yields a new `addItem`, consumed only as an `onClick`, with no effect or cache keyed on it, so no correctness rests on the identity; it is the shape `moveItem` already has from slice 1.

**Bind no longer touching the label — right, both branches.** `bindObject` patches `id`, `type`, `objectName` and clears `object` / `path`; the `isPlaceholder` predicate (`!curLabel`, `'New item'`, `t('engine.appNav.newItem')`) is gone with it. The sentinel branch is dead once nothing births the sentinel. The dropped `''` branch is consistent with the one rule: the runtime reads `''` as present (`resolveLabel('')`), so a legacy `''` shows blank in the console and in the designer alike, and repairing it silently on bind was a second rule keyed on emptiness. The dev's `safeParse` measure at spec 17.5.0 says the entry still parses; the repair path is the Label field (type, then clear → the key is removed). Residual, not a finding: a legacy `''` entry shows an empty Label field with the inherited placeholder, the same look as a label-less one; it is produced only by the pre-fix inspector and was already so on every surface but bind.

**The label-less birth — right.** `addItem` births `{ id: navId, type: 'object' }`; the selection is titled by `navLabel`, which answers the `id`. The birth's validity is unchanged (it lacked `objectName` before too, and completes on bind). Pins re-judged with their intent kept:
- objectui#11189 `navAutosaveFlush`: the rail counter reads `nav_item_N` ids and a save's entries read `{ id }` for a label-less entry; the six assertions (Done sends at once; the clean-buffer control sends nothing; a failed send keeps editing; an in-flight edit lands in the next save; Done waits for it; a re-read keeps the edit) are unchanged.
- objectui#11204 nav case: same counters; the undo-in-flight case still asserts the buffer clean and the save carrying exactly the first add.
- objectui#11167: the presence probe reads `nav_item_3` as text or as the inspector's placeholder.
- objectui#11201: its "New item placeholder bound → no label" case pinned the removed branch; it is replaced by the label-less birth bound to each object (no `label`, parses) plus a legacy "New item" kept verbatim, and the typed-label and locale-map controls stay. Ruling B's intent — bind never adopts the object's label — is kept and now pinned from the birth side.
- objectui#8219 chip pin: the unlabelled leaf reads the inherited `客户` with `object · b2r4_customer` on the tooltip (objectui#7254's reachable half); the `useMetadata` mock gains `objects` as a `vi.hoisted` module-level value.
- `navSurface.test.ts`: "no label carries `''`" now carries `home`, the `pageName` rung; six new resolver cases including the empty-map control.
- `nav-target.test.ts`'s `{ label: 'New item', path: '' }` is the pre-#2245 shape fixture, not a birth reader; untouched, rightly.

**The two removed i18n keys — right.** `engine.appNav.newItem` and `engine.studio.nav.labelPlaceholder` leave both the en and the zh table. A grep of the whole head tree finds no reader of either outside the changeset's own sentence: no source, no test, no `scripts/` list, no doc. Parity between the halves is kept, and `engine.appNav.item` stays for what the rule cannot name.

**Ablations A to D — consistent with the pins, read not re-run.** A: 42 = chip (2) + surface (5) + `navSurface.test.ts` (35); the 6 red are the chip's unlabelled case, the three surface cases and the two resolver-passing cases, while the machine-name, authored and empty-map controls cannot see the ablation. B: 11 = birth (5) + objectui#11189 (6); the 7 red are the two birth cases and the five objectui#11189 cases that count or save an add, the clean-buffer control adding nothing. C: 2 of the 8 in `navItemInspectorLabel`, the two emptying cases. D: 3 of 8, the three placeholder cases.

**Accept set and public surface — nothing moves.** `@object-ui/app-shell` publishes `.` only, and its barrel exports `StudioDesignSurface` and its props but none of `navSurface`, `metadata-admin/i18n`, `AppNavCanvas`, `StudioNavItemInspector` or `InterfacesPillar`; the optional parameters, the `Surface.label` semantics and the two table keys are internal. What the producer writes changes (no `label` on a birth, no `''` drop on bind), but the accept set does not: the spec already accepts a label-less entry (`safeParse` in three pins) and, by the dev's measure, `''`. No schema, prop, type or accepted set moves.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/11196-slice2-surface-inspector-birth.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. The diff touches `packages/app-shell/` only (14 files) plus the changeset, so one package is right, and patch matches what it publishes: a display fix and a producer's birth on internal surfaces. The removed strings are in app-shell's module-local designer table, not the published `@object-ui/i18n` packs (the pending `8754` changeset took `minor` for that public case; this is not that case). Each of the changeset's four claims — caption / breadcrumb / chip inherit however the leaf opens; inspector value, placeholder and clear-removes-the-key; label-less birth with bind untouched, a legacy "New item" kept; two keys removed with no reader — is true of the diff. Pending changesets naming the touched files still hold: `11128` (`AppNavCanvas` shows "Item N" only for what the rule cannot name), `studio-nav-canonical-keys` (`resolveSurface` reads canonical keys only), `8834` (the en ⊆ zh parity). The four changeset gates on the head are success.

`Clause-②: no` — the PR body carries it on line 2, as claim `5915720438` declared, and it holds: no schema, prop, type or accepted set moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `5918098195` names seven deviations and no open question.
1. `i18n.ts` outside the claim — answered, in bounds. The binding direction removes dead i18n keys rather than leaving them; `engine.appNav.newItem` died with the birth and `engine.studio.nav.labelPlaceholder` with the placeholder, and neither has a reader at the head.
2. The falsified `AppNavInspector` premise — answered, confirmed at the head. `AppNavInspector.tsx` is not in the diff, so it equals the base, and it reads neither "New item" nor `engine.appNav.newItem`; its picker never touched the label. Nothing to remove; the claim's plural "pickers'" was wrong by one and the diff is right.
3. The bind's dropped `''` branch — answered in ①; consistent with the one rule, no finding.
4. Re-judged pins beyond the named objectui#11189 file (objectui#11204, #11167, #11201, `navItemInspector.test.tsx`) — answered: within ACCEPT `5915086680`'s answer 3 and the claim's "pins beside each"; each keeps its behavioural assertions (①).
5. The declared narrowing outside the lock (the 15-file readers set and legs C and D, one worker) — a process deviation, declared; the head's check-runs are the run of record for those suites. Not a finding on the diff.
6. The runtime restart at about 18:36Z — nothing ran under the lost hold and the head is one commit. Answered.
7. The model-free commit trailer pair — the repo's own AGENTS.md convention, not a diff matter. Answered.

Carrier-less observations, judged:
- **NavigationDesigner's "New + type" birth labels — a finding the seat MUST file, as a follow-up card, not a FAIL here.** `newNavItem` in `packages/plugin-designer/src/NavigationDesigner.tsx` stores `New Object` / `New Dashboard` / `New Page` as the entry's `label` from `addTopLevel` and `addChild`: the producer-writes-a-placeholder shape this card's answer 3 ruled out for `addItem` ("a producer should not write a placeholder as a stored label"). Slice 1's answer 4 ruled the resolver question only (the machine-name rung), not the birth. `@object-ui/plugin-designer` is a published package, so the reach is any host outside this repo that renders `navigation-designer`; none in-repo, so p3.
